attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his essay, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: A categorical observation about LLMs. The normalised proposition keeps 'never', 'anything' and 'mimicry'. 'Proper' world models is the speaker's own qualifier.

contract.note: Not an ordinary reading. It counts small GPTs trained only on chess games as 'LLMs', though Marcus is talking about general chatbots such as o3 and ChatGPT. It also drops 'proper' by saying a world model need not be robust. Both choices push against the speaker and decide the result.

evidence.note: Genuine, correctly dated preprint: a small chess-trained GPT whose board representation is shown to drive its moves when edited. That model is not a large general-purpose LLM in the ordinary sense, so under a fair reading this is context, not a counterexample.
Language models fine-tuned on Othello learn some board structure but struggle with consecutive moves. The excerpt shows no causal intervention, so it settles neither side.

reviews.rationale: The contract scores the claim on a stretched reading: domain-trained small transformers count as LLMs, and 'proper' is relaxed. Read fairly, as general-purpose LLMs and robust world models, the packet has no causal-intervention evidence either way. e4 concerns a different kind of model, and e5 is mixed and non-causal. So the outcome is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his essay.

semantics.note: Keeps 'by the midgame', 'often', the decline in quality and the illegal moves.

contract.note: Asking for stage-by-stage legality and quality data is reasonable. The June 2025 window is inferred and narrow; it excludes nearby tests of the same models, which the drafter flags.

evidence.note: Acher's May 2025 tests: most o3 and o4-mini games ended on an illegal move, at a median of about 15 moves. That fits the illegal-move half, but it falls before the target window and does not measure any decline in move quality within a game.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs both recurring midgame illegal moves and a measured decline in quality. The only item is from before the window and supports the illegal-move half only loosely. Nothing measures quality by game stage, so the evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own observation. He describes Shwartz's study, but the claim about video comprehension is his.

semantics.note: 'Similar problems' refers back to world-model failures, and the 'especially unusual situations' qualifier is kept. The claim about retrieval is the speaker's interpretation and is not scored.

contract.note: The plain reading, that models miss salient events in unusual videos that humans can see, is fair and ordinary. It does not require proof of the internal mechanism.

evidence.note: The original BlackSwanSuite study, available before the post. In full-video description, models tend to give generic captions and miss the unexpected event, and humans beat every model. On a different task, forecasting, models were competitive.

reviews.rationale: The primary study the speaker cites documents video-language models missing unexpected events in unusual videos, with humans doing better. That meets the support condition. Models doing well on forecasting does not undercut the claim about comprehension. The mechanism stays unproven, as the contract allows.

attribution.note: Marcus's own causal claim. Gleave's jailbreak report is only background to it.

semantics.note: Faithfully states the causal link: instruction failures happen because Claude cannot relate words to a world model.

contract.note: It is fair to require causal evidence that separates the proposed deficit from other explanations. Jailbreak success alone does not show the cause.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure that Claude 4 can still be jailbroken some of the time. It confirms the failure but says nothing about its cause.

Anthropic's own interpretability study of the older Claude 3.5 Haiku. It points to an alternative cause: pressure to finish a coherent sentence. It is narrow and not about the model generation Marcus discusses.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes that jailbreaks happen. No controlled study isolates the proposed missing world model as the cause in the relevant Claude models. e2 suggests another mechanism, but it is a company disclosure about an earlier model, so it decides nothing.
